nodes.name: Music
nodes.description: The art of organizing sound in time through melody, harmony, rhythm, and timbre for expressive, cultural, and aesthetic purposes.

nodes.name: Music Theory
nodes.description: The study of the structural and syntactic elements of music and the principles governing their combination.

nodes.name: Harmony
nodes.description: The study of simultaneous pitches, chord construction, and chord progressions.

nodes.name: Melody
nodes.description: The study of linear sequences of pitches forming a recognizable musical line.

nodes.name: Rhythm
nodes.description: The organization of music in time through beat, meter, tempo, and duration.

nodes.name: Counterpoint
nodes.description: The technique of combining independent melodic lines into coherent polyphonic texture.

nodes.name: Orchestration
nodes.description: The art of assigning musical material to instruments and voices of an ensemble.

nodes.name: Musical Form
nodes.description: The structural organization of a musical work into sections and their arrangement.

nodes.name: Musical Notation
nodes.description: The systems of written symbols used to represent pitch, duration, and performance instructions.

nodes.name: Tuning Systems
nodes.description: The organization of pitch relationships and temperaments underlying a musical tradition.

nodes.name: Timbre
nodes.description: The quality of a sound that distinguishes instruments and voices beyond pitch and loudness.

nodes.name: Music Analysis
nodes.description: The systematic examination of musical works to reveal structure, style, and meaning.

nodes.name: Music History
nodes.description: The historical study of musical practices, repertoires, and their cultural contexts.

nodes.name: Medieval Music
nodes.description: Western sacred and secular music of roughly the 5th to 14th centuries, including plainchant and early polyphony.

nodes.name: Renaissance Music
nodes.description: Western polyphonic music of the 15th to early 17th centuries.

nodes.name: Baroque Music
nodes.description: Western music of c.1600-1750 characterized by figured bass, ornamentation, and contrast.

nodes.name: Classical Period Music
nodes.description: Western music of c.1750-1820 emphasizing clarity, balance, and sonata form.

nodes.name: Romantic Music
nodes.description: Western music of the 19th century emphasizing expression, chromaticism, and programmatic content.

nodes.name: Twentieth-Century Music
nodes.description: Western art music of the 1900s marked by radical expansion of tonality, timbre, and form.

nodes.name: Contemporary Classical Music
nodes.description: Living art-music practice continuing and contesting the traditions of the twentieth century.

nodes.name: Ethnomusicology
nodes.description: The study of music in its social and cultural contexts, especially non-Western and folk traditions.

nodes.name: Classical Music
nodes.description: Western art music of the broad tradition grounded in written scores and formal concert culture.

nodes.name: Symphony
nodes.description: A large-scale multi-movement orchestral work.

nodes.name: Concerto
nodes.description: A work for solo instrument(s) with orchestra, typically in three movements.

nodes.name: Sonata
nodes.description: A multi-movement instrumental work for soloist or small ensemble.

nodes.name: Chamber Music
nodes.description: Instrumental music written for small ensembles of one player per part.

nodes.name: String Quartet
nodes.description: Chamber music for two violins, viola, and cello.

nodes.name: Piano Trio
nodes.description: Chamber music for piano, violin, and cello.

nodes.name: Choral Music
nodes.description: Music composed for ensembles of singers.

nodes.name: Cantata
nodes.description: A vocal work with instrumental accompaniment in several movements, often sacred.

nodes.name: Oratorio
nodes.description: A large unstaged sacred or secular dramatic work for chorus, soloists, and orchestra.

nodes.name: Mass
nodes.description: A musical setting of the Roman Catholic Eucharistic liturgy.

nodes.name: Art Song
nodes.description: A setting of poetry for solo voice and piano, especially the German Lied and French mélodie.

nodes.name: Symphonic Poem
nodes.description: A one-movement orchestral work depicting a narrative, scene, or idea.

nodes.name: Impressionism
nodes.description: Late 19th-early 20th century music using color, non-functional harmony, and atmosphere.

nodes.name: Expressionism
nodes.description: Early 20th century music conveying intense subjectivity through atonality and dissonance.

nodes.name: Serialism
nodes.description: Compositional technique organizing pitches and other parameters into ordered series.

nodes.name: Minimalism
nodes.description: Late 20th century style built on repetition, gradual process, and steady pulse.

nodes.name: Neoclassicism
nodes.description: 20th century style returning to balance and forms of earlier eras within a modern idiom.

nodes.name: Jazz
nodes.description: African-American music centered on improvisation, swing rhythm, and blues-based harmony.

nodes.name: Ragtime
nodes.description: Syncopated piano music of the late 19th and early 20th centuries, a precursor of jazz.

nodes.name: Dixieland
nodes.description: Early New Orleans-style jazz featuring collective improvisation over a front line.

nodes.name: Swing
nodes.description: Big-band jazz of the 1930s-40s built on a propulsive danceable rhythmic feel.

nodes.name: Bebop
nodes.description: Fast, virtuosic 1940s jazz emphasizing complex harmony and small-combo improvisation.

nodes.name: Cool Jazz
nodes.description: Restrained, lyrical 1950s jazz with softer timbres and relaxed tempos.

nodes.name: Hard Bop
nodes.description: Soulful 1950s-60s jazz fusing bebop with blues and gospel influences.

nodes.name: Modal Jazz
nodes.description: Jazz organized around scales (modes) rather than chord progressions.

nodes.name: Free Jazz
nodes.description: Avant-garde jazz abandoning fixed chord changes and regular meter.

nodes.name: Jazz Fusion
nodes.description: Jazz merged with rock, funk, and electronic elements from the late 1960s onward.

nodes.name: Latin Jazz
nodes.description: Jazz incorporating Afro-Cuban and Brazilian rhythms and percussion.

nodes.name: Smooth Jazz
nodes.description: Polished, radio-friendly jazz-pop hybrid popular from the 1980s.

nodes.name: Avant-Garde Jazz
nodes.description: Experimental jazz exploring extended techniques, noise, and non-idiomatic improvisation.

nodes.name: Blues
nodes.description: African-American folk music built on the twelve-bar form, blue notes, and call-and-response.

nodes.name: Delta Blues
nodes.description: Acoustic solo blues of the Mississippi Delta, often slide guitar and voice.

nodes.name: Chicago Blues
nodes.description: Electrified urban blues developed in Chicago after World War II.

nodes.name: Electric Blues
nodes.description: Blues performed on amplified instruments with a full rhythm section.

nodes.name: Popular Music
nodes.description: Commercially oriented music distributed to mass audiences through the recording industry.

nodes.name: Pop Music
nodes.description: Mainstream popular music emphasizing catchy melody, accessible structure, and broad appeal.

nodes.name: Synth-Pop
nodes.description: Pop music built around synthesizers and drum machines, prominent in the 1980s.

nodes.name: Dance-Pop
nodes.description: Up-tempo pop designed for dance, often fusing electronic production with pop hooks.

nodes.name: Teen Pop
nodes.description: Pop marketed primarily to adolescent audiences.

nodes.name: Bubblegum Pop
nodes.description: Lightweight, highly commercial pop of the late 1960s-70s aimed at pre-teens.

nodes.name: K-Pop
nodes.description: Korean popular music blending polished production, choreography, and idol culture.

nodes.name: J-Pop
nodes.description: Japanese popular music spanning idol pop, city pop, and rock-influenced styles.

nodes.name: Rock Music
nodes.description: Electric guitar-driven popular music descended from rock and roll and rhythm and blues.

nodes.name: Rock and Roll
nodes.description: The 1950s fusion of blues, country, and R&B that founded rock music.

nodes.name: Hard Rock
nodes.description: Loud, aggressive rock built on distorted guitar riffs and strong backbeats.

nodes.name: Progressive Rock
nodes.description: Rock of the late 1960s-70s incorporating complex structures and classical influences.

nodes.name: Psychedelic Rock
nodes.description: Rock evoking altered consciousness through effects, drones, and extended improvisation.

nodes.name: Glam Rock
nodes.description: Theatrical 1970s rock emphasizing flamboyant costume and persona.

nodes.name: Punk Rock
nodes.description: Fast, stripped-down, rebellious rock emerging in the mid-1970s.

nodes.name: Post-Punk
nodes.description: Experimental rock of the late 1970s-80s extending punk into artier, darker territory.

nodes.name: New Wave
nodes.description: Poppy, synth-friendly rock of the late 1970s-80s following punk.

nodes.name: Alternative Rock
nodes.description: Broad post-punk rock outside the mainstream that became commercially dominant in the 1990s.

nodes.name: Indie Rock
nodes.description: Rock produced and distributed independently of major labels, with an underground aesthetic.

nodes.name: Grunge
nodes.description: Seattle-based 1990s rock fusing punk energy with heavy, sludgy guitar sound.

nodes.name: Heavy Metal
nodes.description: Aggressive rock emphasizing thick distorted guitar, power, and virtuosity.

nodes.name: Thrash Metal
nodes.description: Fast, aggressive 1980s metal blending punk speed with metal riffing.

nodes.name: Death Metal
nodes.description: Extreme metal featuring growled vocals, blast beats, and low-tuned riffing.

nodes.name: Black Metal
nodes.description: Extreme metal emphasizing tremolo riffing, shrieked vocals, and atmospheric production.

nodes.name: Doom Metal
nodes.description: Slow, heavy metal descended from Black Sabbath's riff-based gloom.

nodes.name: Power Metal
nodes.description: Melodic, fast metal with epic themes and clean high vocals.

nodes.name: Hip-Hop Music
nodes.description: African-American culture and music built on rapping, DJing, breakbeats, and sampling.

nodes.name: Rap
nodes.description: Rhythmic rhymed vocal delivery over a beat.

nodes.name: Gangsta Rap
nodes.description: Hard-edged rap narrating urban street life, prominent from the late 1980s.

nodes.name: Conscious Rap
nodes.description: Rap focused on social, political, and philosophical themes.

nodes.name: Trap
nodes.description: Southern hip-hop style defined by rolling hi-hats, 808 bass, and triplet flows.

nodes.name: Boom Bap
nodes.description: Hard-hitting sample-based 1990s East Coast hip-hop production style.

nodes.name: Drill
nodes.description: Dark, minimalist trap subgenre originating in Chicago in the early 2010s.

nodes.name: Lo-Fi Hip-Hop
nodes.description: Mellow, deliberately imperfect instrumental hip-hop popular as study music.

nodes.name: Rhythm and Blues
nodes.description: African-American popular music rooted in blues and gospel, foundational to rock and soul.

nodes.name: Soul
nodes.description: Gospel-inflected R&B of the 1960s emphasizing passionate vocal delivery.

nodes.name: Funk
nodes.description: Groove-driven music built on syncopated bass and rhythmic interplay.

nodes.name: Contemporary R&B
nodes.description: Modern R&B blending soul vocals with pop, hip-hop, and electronic production.

nodes.name: Neo Soul
nodes.description: 1990s-2000s soul revival emphasizing organic production and jazz influence.

nodes.name: Country Music
nodes.description: American popular music rooted in Southern folk, blues, and Western traditions.

nodes.name: Bluegrass
nodes.description: Acoustic string-band music featuring virtuosic banjo, fiddle, and mandolin.

nodes.name: Western Swing
nodes.description: Dance-oriented 1930s-40s country music blending jazz and big-band swing.

nodes.name: Reggae
nodes.description: Jamaican popular music built on offbeat rhythms and Rastafarian themes.

nodes.name: Ska
nodes.description: Upbeat Jamaican music preceding reggae, emphasizing offbeat guitar and horns.

nodes.name: Rocksteady
nodes.description: Slower Jamaican music bridging ska and reggae in the mid-1960s.

nodes.name: Dub
nodes.description: Instrumental reggae remixes emphasizing echo, reverb, and studio manipulation.

nodes.name: Dancehall
nodes.description: Digitized, rhythm-focused Jamaican music that emerged in the late 1970s.

nodes.name: Latin Music
nodes.description: Popular music of Latin American and Iberian traditions and their diasporas.

nodes.name: Salsa
nodes.description: Afro-Cuban dance music developed in New York in the 1960s-70s.

nodes.name: Samba
nodes.description: Brazilian dance music with syncopated percussion, central to Carnival.

nodes.name: Bossa Nova
nodes.description: Soft Brazilian music blending samba rhythm with jazz harmony.

nodes.name: Tango
nodes.description: Argentine-Uruguayan music and dance of passion and bandoneón-led ensembles.

nodes.name: Cumbia
nodes.description: Colombian-origin dance music spread across Latin America in many regional styles.

nodes.name: Reggaetón
nodes.description: Puerto Rican music fusing reggae, dancehall, and Latin rhythms over dembow beats.

nodes.name: Bachata
nodes.description: Romantic Dominican guitar music and dance.

nodes.name: Afrobeats
nodes.description: Contemporary West African pop fusing highlife, hip-hop, and dance rhythms.

nodes.name: Disco
nodes.description: Dance music of the 1970s built on four-on-the-floor beats and orchestration.

nodes.name: Gospel Music
nodes.description: African-American Christian music emphasizing passionate choir-led worship.

nodes.name: Electronic Music
nodes.description: Music created primarily with electronic instruments, synthesis, and computer processing.

nodes.name: Techno
nodes.description: Repetitive machine-driven dance music born in 1980s Detroit.

nodes.name: House Music
nodes.description: Four-on-the-floor dance music born in 1980s Chicago clubs.

nodes.name: Trance
nodes.description: Euphoric, melodic dance music built on buildups and breakdowns.

nodes.name: Drum and Bass
nodes.description: Fast breakbeat-driven dance music with heavy basslines.

nodes.name: Dubstep
nodes.description: Bass-heavy electronic music featuring half-time rhythms and wobble bass.

nodes.name: Ambient Music
nodes.description: Atmospheric music designed to shape environment and mood rather than demand attention.

nodes.name: Industrial Music
nodes.description: Abrasive electronic music using noise, found sound, and mechanical rhythms.

nodes.name: Electro
nodes.description: Early 1980s electronic funk built on drum machines and robotic vocals.

nodes.name: Electronic Dance Music
nodes.description: Umbrella term for festival-oriented electronic dance styles of the 2010s.

nodes.name: Glitch
nodes.description: Music built from the deliberate use of digital errors and artifacts.

nodes.name: Intelligent Dance Music
nodes.description: Experimental, rhythmically complex electronic music for listening rather than dancing.

nodes.name: Synthwave
nodes.description: Retro electronic music evoking 1980s synthesizer soundtracks and aesthetics.

nodes.name: Traditional Music
nodes.description: Music passed down within communities, expressing cultural, ceremonial, and everyday life.

nodes.name: Folk Music
nodes.description: Community-based music transmitted orally and tied to regional identity.

nodes.name: Celtic Music
nodes.description: Folk traditions of Ireland, Scotland, Wales, and Brittany featuring fiddle, pipes, and harp.

nodes.name: Appalachian Music
nodes.description: Folk music of the Appalachian Mountains blending British ballads and African-American influences.

nodes.name: Klezmer
nodes.description: Instrumental music of Eastern European Jewish tradition, often for celebrations.

nodes.name: Flamenco
nodes.description: Andalusian music and dance of gitano origin featuring cante, toque, and baile.

nodes.name: Fado
nodes.description: Portuguese urban song expressing longing (saudade), accompanied by guitarra.

nodes.name: Indian Classical Music
nodes.description: The two great art-music traditions of India, grounded in raga and tala.

nodes.name: Hindustani Classical Music
nodes.description: North Indian classical music emphasizing improvisation within raga and tala.

nodes.name: Carnatic Music
nodes.description: South Indian classical music emphasizing composed kritis and devotional repertoire.

nodes.name: Chinese Classical Music
nodes.description: Chinese art music traditions including solo zither repertoire and ensemble music.

nodes.name: Guqin Music
nodes.description: The literati solo repertoire of the seven-string zither, a UNESCO-recognized heritage.

nodes.name: Guzheng Music
nodes.description: Music for the Chinese plucked zither with movable bridges.

nodes.name: Japanese Traditional Music
nodes.description: Music of Japanese court, theater, and folk traditions.

nodes.name: Gagaku
nodes.description: Ancient Japanese court music and dance with continental Asian roots.

nodes.name: Honkyoku
nodes.description: Solo shakuhachi repertoire of Zen Buddhist mendicant monks.

nodes.name: Korean Traditional Music
nodes.description: Music of Korean court and folk traditions, including pansori and sanjo.

nodes.name: Pansori
nodes.description: Korean narrative song performed by a vocalist with a drummer.

nodes.name: Persian Classical Music
nodes.description: Iranian art music organized around the radif and dastgah modal systems.

nodes.name: Arabic Music
nodes.description: Music of the Arab world organized around the maqam modal system.

nodes.name: Ottoman Classical Music
nodes.description: Classical court music of the Ottoman Empire organized around the makam system.

nodes.name: Gamelan
nodes.description: Indonesian ensemble music of tuned gongs, metallophones, and drums.

nodes.name: African Traditional Music
nodes.description: Diverse rhythmic and polyphonic music of African peoples, central to ceremony and community.

nodes.name: Indigenous Australian Music
nodes.description: Songlines, didgeridoo, and ceremonial music of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.

nodes.name: Musical Instruments
nodes.description: Objects constructed or adapted to produce musical sound.

nodes.name: String Instruments
nodes.description: Instruments producing sound through vibrating strings.

nodes.name: Violin
nodes.description: A bowed treble string instrument central to Western classical music.

nodes.name: Viola
nodes.description: A bowed alto string instrument tuned a fifth below the violin.

nodes.name: Cello
nodes.description: A bowed tenor-bass string instrument held between the knees.

nodes.name: Double Bass
nodes.description: The largest bowed string instrument, foundational to orchestral and jazz rhythm sections.

nodes.name: Guitar
nodes.description: A fretted six-string plucked instrument ubiquitous across popular music.

nodes.name: Electric Guitar
nodes.description: A guitar using electromagnetic pickups for amplification and distortion.

nodes.name: Bass Guitar
nodes.description: An electric or acoustic low-pitched guitar providing harmonic foundation.

nodes.name: Harp
nodes.description: A plucked instrument with strings perpendicular to the soundboard.

nodes.name: Lute
nodes.description: A plucked pear-shaped instrument of medieval and Renaissance Europe.

nodes.name: Oud
nodes.description: A fretless pear-shaped lute central to Middle Eastern music.

nodes.name: Banjo
nodes.description: A plucked instrument with a drum-like body, central to American folk and bluegrass.

nodes.name: Mandolin
nodes.description: A small plucked instrument with paired strings, tuned like a violin.

nodes.name: Ukulele
nodes.description: A small four-string Hawaiian instrument of Portuguese origin.

nodes.name: Sitar
nodes.description: A long-necked plucked lute with sympathetic strings, central to Hindustani music.

nodes.name: Sarod
nodes.description: A fretless plucked lute of Hindustani classical music.

nodes.name: Veena
nodes.description: A plucked string instrument of South Indian Carnatic music.

nodes.name: Guzheng
nodes.description: A Chinese plucked zither with movable bridges and up to twenty-one strings.

nodes.name: Guqin
nodes.description: A seven-string fretless Chinese zither of the literati tradition.

nodes.name: Pipa
nodes.description: A pear-shaped plucked Chinese lute with a broad repertoire.

nodes.name: Erhu
nodes.description: A two-string bowed Chinese spike fiddle.

nodes.name: Koto
nodes.description: A long Japanese plucked zither with thirteen strings.

nodes.name: Shamisen
nodes.description: A three-string Japanese plucked lute used in theater and folk music.

nodes.name: Woodwind Instruments
nodes.description: Wind instruments producing sound via reed vibration or air across an edge.

nodes.name: Flute
nodes.description: A side-blown edge-tone instrument of metal or wood.

nodes.name: Clarinet
nodes.description: A single-reed cylindrical-bore woodwind with a wide register.

nodes.name: Oboe
nodes.description: A double-reed woodwind with a penetrating, reedy tone.

nodes.name: Bassoon
nodes.description: A low double-reed woodwind with a long folded bore.

nodes.name: Saxophone
nodes.description: A single-reed conical-bore instrument central to jazz and band music.

nodes.name: Recorder
nodes.description: A duct-flute used in early music and education.

nodes.name: Dizi
nodes.description: A transverse Chinese bamboo flute with a buzzing membrane.

nodes.name: Shakuhachi
nodes.description: A Japanese end-blown bamboo flute associated with Zen meditation.

nodes.name: Ney
nodes.description: An end-blown reed flute central to Middle Eastern classical music.

nodes.name: Bagpipes
nodes.description: A reed instrument with an air reservoir bag and drone pipes.

nodes.name: Brass Instruments
nodes.description: Wind instruments sounded by lip vibration into a cup or funnel mouthpiece.

nodes.name: Trumpet
nodes.description: The highest brass instrument, valved or natural.

nodes.name: Trombone
nodes.description: A brass instrument using a sliding tube to change pitch.

nodes.name: French Horn
nodes.description: A coiled brass instrument with a wide bell and mellow tone.

nodes.name: Tuba
nodes.description: The lowest brass instrument, anchoring the bass register.

nodes.name: Percussion Instruments
nodes.description: Instruments sounded by striking, shaking, or scraping.

nodes.name: Timpani
nodes.description: Tunable kettledrums of the orchestra.

nodes.name: Snare Drum
nodes.description: A double-headed drum with snares, central to drum kits and marching bands.

nodes.name: Cymbals
nodes.description: Thin metal plates struck together or with sticks.

nodes.name: Xylophone
nodes.description: A pitched percussion instrument of tuned wooden bars.

nodes.name: Marimba
nodes.description: A deep-toned xylophone with resonators, prominent in Latin American music.

nodes.name: Vibraphone
nodes.description: A metal-bar xylophone with motorized resonators and vibrato.

nodes.name: Tabla
nodes.description: A pair of hand drums central to Hindustani music.

nodes.name: Mridangam
nodes.description: A double-headed barrel drum of South Indian Carnatic music.

nodes.name: Djembe
nodes.description: A goblet-shaped West African drum played with bare hands.

nodes.name: Conga
nodes.description: A tall single-headed Afro-Cuban drum played in sets.

nodes.name: Taiko
nodes.description: Large Japanese drums played in ensemble with choreographed movement.

nodes.name: Steelpan
nodes.description: A tuned percussion instrument made from an oil drum, of Trinidadian origin.

nodes.name: Keyboard Instruments
nodes.description: Instruments played by pressing keys arranged on a keyboard.

nodes.name: Piano
nodes.description: A keyboard instrument whose hammers strike strings, central to Western music.

nodes.name: Organ
nodes.description: A keyboard wind instrument producing sustained tones through pipes.

nodes.name: Harpsichord
nodes.description: A plucked keyboard instrument of the Baroque era.

nodes.name: Accordion
nodes.description: A portable free-reed instrument with bellows and keyboard.

nodes.name: Harmonium
nodes.description: A pump-operated free-reed keyboard widely used in Indian music.

nodes.name: Electronic Instruments
nodes.description: Instruments producing or shaping sound electronically.

nodes.name: Synthesizer
nodes.description: An electronic instrument generating and shaping sounds via oscillators and filters.

nodes.name: Drum Machine
nodes.description: An electronic device programming and playing synthesized percussion patterns.

nodes.name: Sampler
nodes.description: A device that records and plays back audio samples as instruments.

nodes.name: Theremin
nodes.description: An early electronic instrument played by moving hands near two antennas.

nodes.name: Turntable
nodes.description: A record player repurposed as an instrument for scratching in DJ culture.

nodes.name: Vocal Music
nodes.description: Music performed by the human voice, solo or in ensemble.

nodes.name: Choral Singing
nodes.description: Singing in an organized ensemble of voices divided into parts.

nodes.name: A Cappella
nodes.description: Vocal music performed without instrumental accompaniment.

nodes.name: Bel Canto
nodes.description: An Italian operatic singing technique emphasizing beauty of tone and agility.

nodes.name: Throat Singing
nodes.description: Overtone singing producing multiple pitches at once, practiced across Central Asia.

nodes.name: Scat Singing
nodes.description: Jazz vocal improvisation using nonsense syllables as instrumental lines.

nodes.name: Yodeling
nodes.description: Rapid alternation between chest and head voice, traditional to Alpine regions.

nodes.name: Beatboxing
nodes.description: Vocal percussion imitating drum machines and sound effects, part of hip-hop culture.

nodes.name: Music Technology
nodes.description: Technologies for creating, recording, producing, and distributing music.

nodes.name: Sound Recording
nodes.description: The capture and storage of sound for playback and reproduction.

nodes.name: Sound Synthesis
nodes.description: The electronic generation of sound through oscillators, filters, and models.

nodes.name: Sampling
nodes.description: The reuse of recorded audio fragments in new compositions.

nodes.name: Digital Audio Workstation
nodes.description: Software for recording, editing, and producing audio and music.
